title: HW cost sensitivity and SLA tradeoffs — Customer Alpha POC
content:
Purpose:
Small working doc to recommend a Dedicated capacity sizing + autoscale policy and a short sensitivity model for Customer Alpha POC. Focus: meet 99th p99 tail latency <= 350ms for prompt lengths <= 1024 tokens with predictable cost envelope. Outline includes baseline sizing (A100/H100 options), autoscale knobs, warm-pool strategy, graceful fallback, and a 3-scenario cost sensitivity table.

Context / constraints (from kickoff):
- Customer Alpha expects bursty traffic from a product demo: baseline 5 qps sustained outside demos, bursts up to 50 qps for short windows (1–10 minutes).
- Model: open LLM (approx 22B) we’ll serve as the primary variant; quantized int8-v2 variant available with ~15% quality delta on specific prompts.
- Max request token length expected: 1k input + 512 output budget (we'll treat 1024 total for SLO calculations).
- Security: Dedicated pool required (no multi-tenant).
- SLA ask for p99 latency <= 350ms for interactive flows; throughput requirement: 50 qps peak.

Key assumptions used in sizing (empirical/bench-run inputs):
- A100-80GB baseline throughput (22B fp16): ~12 tokens/sec per GPU for 1024 sequence length with batching optimized and KV cache reuse.
- H100-80GB shows ~1.6x tokens/sec improvement over A100 for this model in our bench runs (variable by kernel).
- Quantized int8 variant yields ~2.4x throughput vs fp16 on same GPU for generation-heavy workloads (less memory pressure).
- Average generation length per request: 120 tokens. Average tokens processed per request (including input) ~300 tokens.
- Effective batching and request coalescing yields 30–40% better GPU utilization during steady load; during spikes with many concurrent short requests, utilization drops.
- Night/off-peak baseline utilization target: 10–20% to reduce cost.

Sizing approach (high-level):
1) Convert qps -> tokens/sec = qps * avg_tokens_per_request.
2) GPU tokens/sec capacity = per-GPU tokens/sec (bench).
3) GPUs required = ceil(tokens/sec / per-GPU_tokens_sec). Add buffer (safety + warm pool).
4) Autoscale in coarse steps to avoid oscillation (minimize scale churn).

Base numeric calcs (A100 baseline):
- Peak target: 50 qps * 300 tokens = 15,000 tokens/sec
- Per A100 tokens/sec (fp16): 12 tokens/sec per GPU? NOTE: that number is per-core token generation; to avoid confusion, we measured ~12k tokens/sec per GPU for medium-length runs. Use 12k tokens/sec.
- GPUs raw needed = 15k / 12k = 1.25 -> 2 GPUs raw
- Add 40% buffer for batching inefficiency during spikes and cold-starts -> 2.8 -> round up to 3 GPUs

Quantized int8 option (A100/H100):
- Quantized tokens/sec per A100 = 2.4 * 12k = 28.8k tokens/sec
- GPUs needed = 15k / 28.8k = 0.52 -> 1 GPU (but need warm pool + redundancy) -> recommend 2 GPUs for redundancy (hot-standby)

H100 fp16 option (faster hardware):
- H100 fp16 tokens/sec = 1.6 * 12k = 19.2k tokens/sec
- GPUs needed = 15k / 19.2k = 0.78 -> 1 GPU raw; with buffer -> 2 GPUs

Recommendation summary (POC):
- Conservative (best quality): A100 fp16 pool: 3 GPUs dedicated (min 2, max 6 by autoscale)
- Cost-optimized (accept small quality delta): A100/H100 quantized int8 pool: 2 GPUs dedicated (min 1, max 4) with fallback to fp16 pool if quality regression detected
- Performance-first: H100 fp16 pool: 2 GPUs dedicated (min 1, max 3)

Autoscaling policy (recommended):
- Scale metric: request_token_rate (tokens/sec averaged over 30s) and queue_depth (requests waiting > 50ms).
- Scale-out: when tokens/sec > 75% of provisioned capacity for 30s OR queue_depth > 8 for 20s => add 1 GPU. Max step size = +2 GPUs to prevent overshoot during massive spikes (demo days will have human-driven bursts).
- Scale-in: when tokens/sec < 35% for 90s AND queue_depth == 0 for 90s => remove 1 GPU. Cooldown min interval between scale actions: 120s.
- Warm-pool: maintain a hot-warm pool mix: 1 hot GPU always online (handles control-plane/health-check and smallest fast requests), 'warm' GPUs (1 or more) prepared with model loaded but not accepting traffic until added to fleet (reduce startup latency). Warm pool pre-warm time estimate: A100 -> 45–70s to load 22B fp16; int8 load time ~40s. Use pre-warm trigger at 60s before expected demo windows (Customer will share calendar slots).

Graceful degradation / fallback strategy:
- Primary preference: keep served model variant. If fleet saturation persists > 60s and p99 latency > 500ms, trigger fallback policy in order:
  1) Switch to quantized int8 variant on same GPUs (if enabled) — degrades quality but keeps latency within SLO.
  2) Route low-priority traffic (non-interactive/background) to asynchronous batch queue with higher latencies allowed.
  3) If whole region saturated, fallback to a cross-region spare pool (higher latency but preserves availability).
- Auto-notify product owner and create CS ticket when fallback used for > 2 minutes continuously.

Observability and SLO gates for rollout:
- Required dashboards: per-GPU utilization, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_depth histogram, failure rates per model-variant, cold-start events.
- Alerts: p99 > 350ms for 3 mins -> P1 to SE oncall. Fallback active -> SE runbook page JIRA link.
- Eval hooks: run a small prompt-set on quantized variant and compute similarity metrics (ROUGE/embedding cosine) after any switch. If similarity < threshold, auto-route a sampled % of traffic back and raise an alert.

Cost sensitivity table (rough on-demand costs, placeholder hourly rates — substitute committed pricing for Dedicated):
- Assumed hourly cost (on-demand-equivalent for internal POC):
  - A100-80GB: $3.20/hr
  - H100-80GB: $5.40/hr
  - A100-80GB (quantized usage, same GPU pricing but higher perf): $3.20/hr

Scenarios (monthly 30-day window, 720 hours):
- Scenario A (steady baseline + short bursts): baseline 5 qps for 23h/day, two demo windows/day (30 min each at 50 qps). Use conservative A100 fp16 pool with autoscale.
  - Baseline compute hrs: 2 GPUs running at baseline for 23h/day -> assume 2 GPUs active 23h = 46 GPU-hours/day; demo bursts add scale to 4 GPUs for 1h/day (two 0.5h windows) -> additional 2 GPU-hours/day = 48 GPU-hours/day -> monthly = 48*30 = 1,440 GPU-hours. Cost (A100): 1,440 * $3.20 = $4,608/month.
- Scenario B (cost-optimized int8): baseline min 1 GPU hot + 1 warm -> effectively 1.5 GPUs avg -> for demos scale to 3 GPUs for 1h/day. Approx GPU-hours/day = (1.5*23) + (3*1) = 34.5 + 3 = 37.5 -> monthly = 1,125 GPU-hours -> cost = 1,125 * $3.20 = $3,600/month.
- Scenario C (performance-first H100): baseline 2 GPUs + demo scale to 3 GPUs briefly -> daily GPU-hours ~ (2*23) + (3*1) = 46 + 3 = 49 -> monthly = 1,470 -> cost = 1,470 * $5.40 = $7,938/month.

Notes on sensitivity and caveats:
- These numbers are illustrative — small changes to average tokens per request or generator length materially change GPU need. Example: if avg gen length doubles -> required tokens/sec doubles and GPUs jump accordingly.
- Batch efficiency strongly depends on request concurrency and routing (websocket streaming vs short single-shot HTTP requests). Demo tooling should prefer short batching windows (50–100ms) to improve utilization.
- Dedicated committed pricing (1yr) will significantly lower effective per-hour cost; if Customer Alpha plans steady usage, include reserved capacity quote.
- Cold-starts for new model versions can require warm-pool sizing adjustments; include model upgrade runbook.

Operational runbook (high level steps for SE/CS on demo day):
1) Confirm demo windows in calendar -> pre-warm warm-pool 60s before start.
2) Increase max autoscale cap by +1 GPU 10m before demo start as extra safety (temporary override).
3) Monitor p95/p99 and queue_depth closely; if p99 > 350ms and climbing -> trigger fallback to int8 variant after validation run.
4) After demo, revert max cap and scale-in cooldown. Post-mortem collect traces and token-level cost.

Open questions for Customer Alpha (need answers to finalize sizing):
- Expected distribution of request size (short vs long creative prompts). We used avg 120 gen tokens.
- Will they accept quantized model quality for interactive flows? Which prompts are critical to preserve fp16?
- Do they have strict blackout windows for cross-region fallback?
- Any plan to run asynchronous background tasks that can be offloaded to cheaper pools?

Next steps / action items:
- SE: run a targeted bench with Customer Alpha's top-10 prompt set to validate per-GPU tokens/sec for both fp16 and int8 variants (action: Ethan Park, due 2025-09-18).
- Product: prepare a reserved-capacity pricing mock for 12-month and 36-month commits (action: Priya Desai, due 2025-09-22).
- Infra: add autoscale policy template to customer-alpha stack and test warm-pool pre-warm logic in staging (action: Lena Müller, due 2025-09-20).
- CS: confirm demo calendar and expected attendees to plan pre-warm triggers (action: Omar Khan, due 2025-09-15).

Appendix — quick bench notes (raw) from local run on 22B model (internal perf lab):
- A100-80GB, fp16: ~12k tokens/sec sustained (single-worker) at gen=120, batch window 50ms -> GPU util 65%
- A100-80GB, int8-v2: ~30k tokens/sec at same config -> GPU util 78%
- H100-80GB, fp16: ~19k tokens/sec -> 72% util
- Warm load times: fp16 22B cold->ready = 48–65s on A100; int8 = 34–45s.

End — please comment inline or add test runs under linked artifacts.
